samples.summary: Unbounded comment body is mention-parsed server-side with an O(n²) dedupe on the request path — one authenticated POST can block the Node event loop (backend-wide DoS)
samples.evidence: `createThread`/`reply` validate the body only with `normalizeBody` (comments.controller.ts:270, 357), which checks `typeof raw === 'string'` and a non-empty trim — there is no length cap, and because the handler takes `@Body() body: unknown` the global ValidationPipe (`main.ts:65`) has no DTO to enforce one. The Express JSON limit is 25 MB (`main.ts:20`). After the CRDT write, `notify()` awaits `planCommentNotifications` (comments.controller.ts:198), which calls `extractMentionedUserIds` in `packages/sheets/src/comment/mentions.ts` — that function de-duplicates with `!ids.includes(segment.userId)`, i.e. a linear scan per mention, so n distinct `@[a](N)` tokens cost O(n²) synchronous comparisons. Attack: any workspace member (or any write-scoped API key) POSTs `/api/v1/workspaces/{ws}/documents/{doc}/comments` with a ~5 MB body of ~500k distinct mention tokens; `extractMentionedUserIds` then runs ~10^11 comparisons on the single-threaded event loop, stalling every other request in the process, and the request is repeatable up to the 120/min global IP throttle (app.module.ts:102). This parsing is new here — the frontend runs the identical planner in the author's own browser, and the pre-existing `POST /notifications/comment` never parses a body at all (it receives an already-validated `recipientUserIds` array).

samples.summary: Direct `createFromComment` call bypasses the `CommentNotificationDto` validation (ArrayMaxSize/MaxLength) that the equivalent HTTP route enforces; an uncapped recipient list reaches a Prisma `IN` query
samples.evidence: `this.notificationService.createFromComment(actorId, plan)` (comments.controller.ts:207) is fed a plan built in-process and merely cast — `planCommentNotifications(...) as CommentNotificationDto[]` (line 204). The only other caller, `NotificationController.createFromComment` (notification/notification.controller.ts:63-71), receives a real `CommentNotificationDto`, so the global ValidationPipe applies `@ArrayMaxSize(50)` to `recipientUserIds`, `@MaxLength(200)` to `threadId`/`commentId` and `@MaxLength(2000)` to `preview` (notification.dto.ts:42-67). None of those bounds exist on the new path. Consequence: `recipientUserIds` is whatever the comment body's mention tokens produce (unbounded — `notify-plan.ts` applies no cap), and `createFromComment` passes the *whole* candidate list to `memberIdsAmong` → `prisma.workspaceMember.findMany({ where: { userId: { in: ... } } })` (notification.service.ts:126-129, 432-435) **before** the `MAX_RECIPIENTS` slice at line 138, so a body with tens of thousands of mentions becomes a single enormous `IN (...)` (past pg's 65535 bind-parameter ceiling). Likewise `threadId` comes from the URL/CRDT and is written to `Notification.threadId`/`dedupeKey` with no length bound. The validation was not weakened in place — it was routed around by a second writer, which is exactly the pattern that reads as covered.

samples.summary: `UserThrottlerGuard` (30 notification reports/min/user) is bypassed by the new notification writer, and the design doc's stated justification for that is inaccurate for `comment_mention`
samples.evidence: `POST /notifications/comment` is deliberately rate-limited per *user* at 30/min (notification.controller.ts:63-65, `@UseGuards(UserThrottlerGuard) @Throttle({limit:30})`) because, per its own docblock, "this is the one endpoint a client can call on its own initiative". The comment routes are now a second such surface and mount only the global per-IP `ThrottlerGuard` (120/min, app.module.ts:102) — 4× the per-minute notification volume, and keyed on IP rather than on the caller, so it does not bound a user at all. `docs/design/notifications.md` (added paragraph, ~line 240) justifies the omission with "each verb notifies at most the thread's participants"; that is true for `comment_reply`/`thread_resolved` but false for `comment_mention`, whose `recipientUserIds` come from mention tokens in the attacker-supplied body and are capped only by `MAX_RECIPIENTS` (20) inside the service. Net effect: a workspace member can push up to ~2400 notification rows/min into other members' inboxes with attacker-chosen preview text, versus 600/min through the throttled path. Searched: `UserThrottlerGuard` usages (notification.controller.ts, template.controller.ts only), `@Throttle` decorators across backend/src, and app.module's single global throttler.
searchedFor: read docs/design/notifications.md hunk in the diff

samples.summary: `parseImages` accepts any string as `SheetImage.src` — no scheme or origin allowlist on a value the server now stores on behalf of a caller and every viewer's browser then fetches
samples.evidence: `src: requireString(i.src, 'src')` (worksheet-images.ts:55) validates only non-emptiness, and the docblock states it is "stored verbatim". The controller writes it into the CRDT (`worksheet-images.controller.ts`, `ws.images[image.id] = image`), and `image-object-layer.tsx:216` renders it as `` after `resolveImageSrc`, whose contract explicitly leaves "`data:`, `blob:`, external" URLs untouched (image-cache.ts:31-32). So a write-scoped API key can plant `https://attacker.example/beacon.png` (or a large `data:` blob) that every collaborator who opens the sheet fetches — viewer IP/UA disclosure to a third party, chosen by someone who never touched a browser. The codebase already treats a hostile CRDT `src` as an expected threat and defends the worst consequence (`isTrustedWorkspaceImageUrl` in frontend/src/api/share-image-url.ts:27 stops the share token leaking; `parseImageRef` in document-image-refs.ts:66 refuses foreign origins), which is why the missing normalization at the one server-mediated write path is worth noting rather than assuming the editor is the only writer. Impact is bounded because a malicious editor client could already write the same value straight into the CRDT — hence minor, not major.

samples.summary: Caller-supplied image `id` is used directly as a record key with no `__proto__`/`constructor` rejection, unlike tab ids which this same change routes through `safeWorksheetRecordKeys`
samples.evidence: `parseImages` requires only a non-empty string id (worksheet-images.ts:54) and `setImages` then does `ws.images = {}; for (const image of images) ws.images[image.id] = image;`. With `id === "__proto__"` the assignment hits the prototype setter instead of creating an own property: on a plain-object root the entry silently vanishes and the map's `[[Prototype]]` becomes the caller's object. The same key later survives into a JSON snapshot as an ordinary own property and reaches `reviveLongs` in document/document-copy.service.ts:590-593, whose `const out: JsonRoot = {}; out[key] = ...` loop is the identical unguarded gadget — `rewriteImageRefs` (document-image-refs.ts:214) uses `Object.create(null)` precisely because `JSON.parse` can produce a `__proto__` own key, so the hazard is already acknowledged elsewhere in the tree. This is not global `Object.prototype` pollution, which is why I rate it minor; but it is an unvalidated caller-controlled record key on a path where this very change added a careful key-membership guard (`worksheet-lookup.util.ts`) for exactly the analogous tab-id case, and the asymmetry looks unintentional.

verdict.reason: Every element of the claimed chain is present as described. `normalizeBody` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/comment-ops.ts:389-392) enforces only `typeof raw === 'string'` plus a non-empty trim — no length cap — and both write handlers declare `@Body() body: unknown` (comments.controller.ts:265, 353), so the global ValidationPipe (main.ts:65-72) has no DTO metatype to enforce one; the Express JSON cap is 25 MB (main.ts:20, applied at :48-57). After the CRDT write, `createThread` (:309, :341) and `reply` (:372) await `notify()`, which synchronously calls `planCommentNotifications` (comments.controller.ts:198) -> `extractMentionedUserIds(comment.body)` (packages/sheets/src/comment/notify-plan.ts:109). That function de-duplicates with `!ids.includes(segment.userId)` (packages/sheets/src/comment/mentions.ts:86), a linear scan per mention, so n distinct `@[](id)` tokens cost ~n^2/2 synchronous comparisons on the single-threaded event loop before the response returns. The `toNotifiableUserId` filter runs only after the dedupe (notify-plan.ts:110-111), so it does not bound the cost, and MAX_COMMENT_PREVIEW_LENGTH (notify-plan.ts:41) truncates only the stored preview, after the parse. I grepped for any comment-body length limit and found none anywhere in the repo — the only `assertNonEmpty` helpers (packages/sheets/src/comment/thread.ts:3, packages/frontend/src/components/comments/thread.ts:8) are emptiness checks on other code paths. Requests are repeatable under the single 120/min throttler bucket (app.module.ts:97-104). No guard makes this unreachable; the only residual uncertainty is whether a multi-megabyte Yorkie write might fail first, but an attacker can tune the body smaller (~500 KB -> ~70k tokens -> ~2.5e9 comparisons) and still stall the loop, so that does not refute it. Unvalidated attacker-controlled input driving super-linear synchronous work on a shared event loop is unsafe input handling within the security lens.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. comments.controller.ts:204 casts planCommentNotifications(...) to CommentNotificationDto[] (a compile-time cast only) and calls notificationService.createFromComment at line 207 with no runtime validation; the global ValidationPipe (main.ts:65-70) only applies to the HTTP route notification.controller.ts:66-70. The DTO bounds it bypasses are real (notification.dto.ts:42,54,59,66: @MaxLength(200) threadId/commentId, @ArrayMaxSize(50) recipientUserIds, @MaxLength(2000) preview). In notification.service.ts:123-129 the full candidate list is handed to memberIdsAmong, which at 432-435 runs prisma.workspaceMember.findMany({ where: { userId: { in: unique(userIds) } } }) BEFORE the MAX_RECIPIENTS slice at line 138 — so the service cap does not bound the IN list, contrary to the assumption stated in notify-plan.ts:17-19. Recipient ids come from extractMentionedUserIds (notify-plan.ts:109-111, mentions.ts:83-91) with no cap, and normalizeBody (comment-ops.ts:389-392) imposes no body length limit under a 25mb body-parser limit (main.ts:20,49-50). I enumerated all callers of createFromComment: only the validated HTTP controller and this unvalidated one; the try/catch at comments.controller.ts:208-214 swallows the error but does not prevent the oversized query. Attacker-controlled unbounded input reaching a DB query is an availability/unsafe-input-handling weakness inside the Security lane; no named refutation ground applies.

finding.summary: The same `:tabId` truthiness guard is unfixed in every other worksheet tab controller; the images-controller guard makes the class read as handled while these routes still write through a prototype/proxy key
finding.evidence:
`worksheetOrThrow` in worksheet-rules.controller.ts:55-62 is byte-identical to the pre-fix images version (`const worksheet = root.sheets?.[tabId]; if (!worksheet) throw new NotFoundException(...)`) and line 99 writes straight through it: `this.worksheetOrThrow(root, tabId).conditionalFormats = rules;` with `rules` fully attacker-supplied.

Same unguarded shape at: worksheet-styles.controller.ts:55 (write at :94 `.rangeStyles = rangeStyles`), worksheet-dimensions.controller.ts:58 (writes at :136/:181/:226/:271), worksheet-charts.controller.ts:50 (write at :106), worksheet-filter-pivot.controller.ts:48 (:90/:136), worksheet.controller.ts:48 (:85/:131/:178), cells.controller.ts:89/:126/:159/:194/:231.

Vector, per the proxy behaviour documented at worksheet-structure.controller.ts:84-90: `PUT /api/v1/workspaces/:ws/documents/:doc/tabs/toString/conditional-formats` passes the guard (the trap returns a truthy function) and assigns caller-controlled `rules` onto that object, answering 200 for a write that never lands. On any plain-object root, `sheets['__proto__']` is `Object.prototype` and the same line writes `Object.prototype.conditionalFormats` — process-wide prototype pollution, which is precisely the failure the images controller just added a guard for. Only worksheet-structure.controller.ts uses the correct `safeWorksheetRecordKeys(...).includes(tabId)` check; the fix should be that helper applied uniformly, not a per-controller denylist.

verdict.reason: The described code does not exist. `worksheet-rules.controller.ts:21` imports `worksheetOrThrow` from `./worksheet-lookup.util` rather than defining a local truthiness guard; lines 55-62 are the body of `getConditionalFormats` and the write is at line 83, not 99. The single shared `worksheetOrThrow`/`findWorksheet` in `worksheet-lookup.util.ts:36-59` already performs the exact membership test the finding prescribes — `if (!sheets || !safeWorksheetRecordKeys(sheets).includes(tabId)) return undefined;` (line 41) with a 404 throw at line 57 — and its doc comment (lines 4-34) explicitly covers both the plain-object `__proto__` case and the Yorkie proxy `toJSON`/`getID`/`toString` trap case. `safeWorksheetRecordKeys` (packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-record.ts:33-45) returns `Object.keys`, i.e. own enumerable keys only, so `__proto__` and proxy trap names can never be members. Every controller the finding lists as "unguarded" imports and uses that same helper at the cited lines: worksheet-styles 17/53/79/120, worksheet-dimensions 16/98/118/161/204/247, worksheet-charts 12/68/88, worksheet-filter-pivot 11/46/72/119, worksheet.controller 14/73/120/167, cells 29/89/125/158/192/228. The premise that the fix is a per-controller denylist applied only to images (and structure) is false — it is a shared util already applied uniformly, which is the remediation the finding requests.
